item.title: [7] Observation of gapped Dirac magnons in a Co bilayer grown on Ru(0001)
item.description:
Last authors: Arthur Ernst, Christopher Hins

Authors: Khalil Zakeri, Arthur Ernst, Christopher Hins

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of Dirac magnons; relates to topological and Dirac physics interest.

Tags: #material #Dirac #magnon

Abstract: Long celebrated in graphene, Dirac physics inspires the search for similar phenomena in magnonic systems. Here, the authors experimentally demonstrate that magnons in an epitaxial Co bilayer on Ru(0001) exhibit Dirac properties near the Brillouin zone corner. Remarkably, the substrate does not destroy the essential physics; despite breaking sublattice symmetry and opening a gap, local valley topology remains intact. Beyond opening possibilities for discovering Dirac magnons in other ultrathin 3 d magnetic films, these findings hold promise for on-chip magnonic applications.

item.title: [7] Dynamical magnetism in the disordered cubic lattice material γ−Ba3CoNb2O9
item.description:
Last authors: A. T. M. Nazmul Islam, Bella Lake

Authors: Fanjun Xu, Ralf Feyerherm, Cecilie Glittum, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental neutron/muon study of correlated spins and quantum spin liquid-like behavior.

Tags: #spin-liquid #magnetism #neutron

Abstract: Strong disorder normally favors spin-glass freezing. Here, in contrast, the authors report an unconventional, highly fluctuating spin state in cubic γ-Ba 3 CoNb 2 O 9 with effective spin-½ moments randomly diluted to just above the percolation limit. Neutron and muon measurements, with partially overlapping time windows, surprisingly reveal persistent correlated spin fluctuations from picoseconds to microseconds—a behavior reminiscent of quantum spin liquids. Numerical calculations suggest singlet formation is important. These results show disorder can sustain dynamic spin correlations even without strong geometrical frustration.

item.title: [7] Magnetic symmetry implications of the zero- and applied-field Hall effect of UNi4B
item.description:
Last authors: F. Ronning, E. D. Bauer

Authors: Z. W. Riedel, W. S. Simeth, S. M. Thomas, F. Ronning, E. D. Bauer

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of Hall effect and magnetic symmetry in a heavy-fermion-like system.

Tags: #magnetism #Halleffect #heavyfermion

Abstract: The authors report here two finite zero-field Hall resistivity tensor components associated with the debated magnetic ground state of the noncollinear antiferromagnet UNi 4 B. For a commensurate magnetic structure, the finite Hall resistivity components cannot be explained by the formation of magnetic domains but are compatible with a monoclinic magnetic symmetry lower than that of previously proposed magnetic ordering models. Additional field-dependent Hall resistivity data collected up to 16 T suggest a notable intrinsic contribution to the anomalous Hall effect.

item.title: [7] Coupled dynamical Boltzmann transport equations with long-range electron-phonon and electron-electron interactions in two-dimensional materials
item.description:
Last authors: Francesco Macheda, Thibault Sohier

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Methodological advancement in 2D transport, relevant to ongoing study of 2D materials.

Tags: #transport #monolayer #heterostructure

Abstract: The intrinsic resistivity of materials depends on the interplay of current-carrying electrons with vibrational and electronic excitations. Here, the authors develop a numerical solution to the coupled dynamics of electrons and electrodynamic modes, for 2D monolayers and heterostructures, which includes both types of excitations. They show that while resistivity is ultimately driven by phonons, electronic excitations can play a significant role via direct electron-electron scattering and dynamical screening of the phonons.

item.title: [8] Anatomy of spin-orbit torques in monolayer Fe3GeTe2 and Fe3GaTe2: Insights from atomistic and momentum-space decompositions
item.description:
Last authors: Yaroslav Zhumagulov, Jaroslav Fabian

Authors: Gusthavo M. S. Brizolla, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Yaroslav Zhumagulov, Jaroslav Fabian

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant study of magnetism and momentum-space properties in 2D van der Waals materials.

Tags: #vanderWaals #spintronics #DFT

Abstract: Spin–orbit torque (SOT) enables electrical magnetization control in spintronic devices. Here, the authors calculate SOT in monolayer Fe 3 GeTe 2 and Fe 3 GaTe 2 , van der Waals ferromagnets with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and no reliance on heavy atoms for strong spin–orbit coupling. Horizontal mirror symmetry forbids conventional in-plane spin accumulation for out-of-plane magnetization, while tilting the magnetization enables a strongly angle-dependent response. Combining density functional theory, Wannier interpolation, and Kubo formalism, they map the torque across the magnetization sphere. They reveal hidden torques on mirror-related Fe atoms up to 30 times the net torque, whose cancellation could be lifted through van der Waals engineering.
